name: Shadow Puppet Theatre
summary: Cut-paper silhouettes on a tinted screen: a heron stands in the river of a metric and sees the waterfall first; a human lifts the Roll back lantern.
look: Pure black cut-paper silhouettes with filigree frames against glowing tinted backlights (amber, teal, dawn); one coral light source for the anomaly and the decision.

components.name: Heron silhouette
components.role: Pulse: a still, patient watcher that moves only when it matters

components.name: Tinted backlight
components.role: amber = before, teal = Pulse is watching, dawn = resolved

components.name: Cut-paper towers
components.role: dashboards as a silhouette city with lit window-bars

components.name: River metric
components.role: the metric line as water; the anomaly is a waterfall

components.name: Cartouche
components.role: ornate black label for the anomaly readout

components.name: Coral lantern
components.role: the human’s action (Roll back) glowing in the dark

motion.name: Stepped cut-out poses
motion.how: joints swap between 3 drawn poses at 12 fps, never tweened; pose changes land on quarter notes (0.5 s at 120 BPM)

motion.name: Multiplane drift
motion.how: 3 silhouette layers parallax at 0.3/0.6/1.0 speed, 8-bar loop, linear — the calm under the beat

motion.name: Tint cross-fade
motion.how: background gradient shifts hue over exactly 1 bar (2 s), starting on the drop and on the resolution

story: Hook: a silhouette city of dashboard towers dwarfs a tiny figure — 'How many dashboards did you check today?'. Reveal: the tint turns teal, a moon rises with the Acme mark and a heron opens its wings above 'Acme Pulse'. Proof: the river of the metric falls (checkout −18% since 09:42 after deploy #2231), the heron's neck shoots forward and a human reaches for the glowing Roll back lantern. CTA: dawn, the heron flies, 'Caught before customers noticed.' and Start free.
adapt: Cut your product’s key screens into silhouettes (towers, rivers, paths), pick a watchful animal for your agent, and colour the backlight with your palette to mark each story beat.

references.note: the pioneer of silhouette animation; gesture instead of faces
1926 feature: cut-outs under a camera, multiplane, colour tinting

fit.risk: Silhouette-only frames hide UI detail and can feel slow or melancholy; keep the data in the cartouche large and crisp, and keep the tempo up with stepped poses.
